blocks.text: If f,g are continuous on \([a,b]\), differentiable on \((a,b)\), and \(g\prime\ne0\) there, then \([f(b)-f(a)]/[g(b)-g(a)]=f\prime(c)/g\prime(c)\) for some \(a<c<b\).

items.title: Square root and reciprocal square root
paragraphs: The functions are continuous and differentiable on the positive interval, and \(g\prime(x)=-1/(2x^{3/2})\ne0\).

items.title: Exercise: logarithm and square
question_paragraphs: For \(0<a<b\), show that \(\dfrac{\log b-\log a}{b-a}=\dfrac{a+b}{2c^2}\) for some \(a<c<b\).
paragraphs: Apply CMVT to \(f(x)=\log x,g(x)=x^2\). Its hypotheses hold because x>0 and \(g\prime(x)=2x\ne0\).
